_meta.description: Compact index for task-aware knowledge injection. Each entry has keywords for matching and a one-liner for injection.
_meta.usage: src/lib/knowledge-router.ts reads this file at startup and matches task text against keywords.

entries.oneliner: Context learning works for environmental knowledge only — derivable facts have zero impact (EXP-001)
Text rules have 0% success for judgment failures — 0/20 experiments. Use workflows instead (KE-007)
Rich delegation context (file paths, constraints, verification) reduces wasted ops by 47%
Guards are brittle (false positives when env changes) — use context.md for environmental constraints
QA catches only 14% of issues vs evaluator's 27% — QA rubber-stamps
Skills targeting reasoning patterns don't change tool-calling patterns — behavior at tool-call level is unaffected
Workflow enforcement is the ONLY reliable behavioral intervention — 5/56 experiments promoted, all structural
Heartbeat step restructuring causes regression — don't change heartbeat step order
Negative examples in LESSONS.md have zero effect on behavior
Most gym scenarios hit ceiling — agents pass at baseline. Check baseline before building interventions
Knowledge files are passive — agents skip them in oneshot mode. Critical info must be injected or in context.md
Lab-fork null-patch test confirms infrastructure validity — null patch shows no effect, real patches can be trusted
Task boundedness is the primary driver of delegated session quality — bounded tasks succeed, open-ended fail
Bash quote splitting can bypass security checks — sanitize tool input before shell execution
Decision topology R predicts workflow effectiveness — workflows help when R > 0.5, hurt when R < 0.3
Workflow effectiveness depends on decision type — eliminable decisions benefit, essential decisions don't
Materialize-findings skill improves both behavior AND product quality — write findings before producing output
Environmental nudges match text skills for behavioral change — context.md is as effective as skill files
Sycophancy requires materialization gates (L5) — nudges and basic workflows insufficient
